transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel constantly on edge at the plant and even around loud machines anywhere, like I can’t ever relax or let my guard down. My family doctor referred me to you after I had a really difficult time during a safety walk-through at work recently.
Did these feelings of being on edge start after a specific, frightening event or accident that happened at the plant or around machinery?

Yes, it all started about two and a half years ago when I witnessed a horrific accident at the plant. My coworker and close friend was caught in a malfunctioning press right in front of me, and ever since that day, I just haven't been able to relax around machinery or at work.
Do you ever experience upsetting memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the accident that you can't seem to stop?

Yes, out of nowhere, even when I'm just washing dishes, I'll suddenly see him crushed in that machine as if it's happening all over again. My chest tightens, my hands sweat, and I feel like I'm right back on that floor hearing him scream and the alarms blaring. It is incredibly vivid and I just can't seem to stop it.
Do you find yourself actively trying to avoid thoughts, conversations, or places that remind you of that tragic accident?

Yes, absolutely. I go completely out of my way to avoid walking past the new press line at work and have turned down extra shifts just to stay away. I even had to quit my community theater group because the sound of power tools and the smell of machine oil make me feel like I’m going to fall apart, so avoiding it all is the only way I can cope.
Have you also been experiencing trouble sleeping, irritability, or finding yourself easily startled by sudden noises since the accident?

Yes, I've been struggling with all of those. I lie awake for hours replaying everything and wake up at any little noise, and I've been snapping at my coworkers over minor things and feeling so ashamed afterward. I'm also constantly on edge, flinching at loud sounds and scanning for exits even when I'm just at church or the grocery store.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were [F43.1, F40.2]. The patient's presentation of severe intrusive memories (flashbacks), active avoidance of trauma-related stimuli, hyperarousal (sleep disturbance, irritability, exaggerated startle), and hypervigilance, all starting after witnessing a horrific workplace accident 2.5 years ago, meets the full diagnostic criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1). Specific phobia (F40.2) is ruled out as the primary diagnosis because the avoidance and anxiety are part of the broader PTSD syndrome.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all diagnostic criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD, ICD-10 F43.1). He experienced a qualifying traumatic stressor (witnessing a coworker/friend get crushed in a malfunctioning press 2.5 years ago). He reports persistent intrusion symptoms (vivid flashbacks with physiological reactivity), persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the trauma (avoiding the press line, turning down shifts, quitting community theater), and marked alterations in arousal and reactivity (insomnia, irritability, hypervigilance, and exaggerated startle response). Symptoms have persisted for over two years, causing significant functional impairment.
